review.reason: 리뷰 거절: internal/httpapi/sourcing.go:311 `in.Currency = tenderCurrency` overwrites the stored currency of an existing bid unconditionally, and the ON CONFLICT branch writes `currency=excluded.currency`, so the unit of an already-stored amount is rewritten while the number is left alone. The legacy row this hits is the exact one the commit message exists because of: the old form offered KRW/USD/EUR/JPY and every tender created through the UI is KRW (web/src/pages/Objects.tsx:699 hardcodes it), so a bid stored as USD 50,000 against a KRW tender is the normal pre-change state. On the next save that row silently becomes KRW 50,000. Nothing warns the bidder or the buyer, there is no backfill, and the mismatch guard at sourcing.go:308 cannot catch it because the client now sends the tender's own code. / web/src/pages/Portal.tsx:779 `const currency = item.currency || "KRW"` takes the tender's code and ignores `response.currency`, so for that same legacy bid the form renders `총 견적금액 (KRW)` (Portal.tsx:820) directly above `defaultValue={response?.totalAmount}` = 50000, a number that was dollars. Before this change the box showed the bid's own currency (`defaultValue={response?.currency || "KRW"}`). This is a new, user-visible mislabeling of an existing amount, and it is what feeds the silent rewrite above. / internal/httpapi/currency_integration_test.go:23 the new integration test only covers a tender in USD with no prior bid; it never seeds a response whose currency differs from the tender's, which is the only case where the overwrite at sourcing.go:311 does anything. The behaviour that regressed is not exercised by any test in this branch.

reasons: internal/httpapi/sourcing.go:311 `in.Currency = tenderCurrency` overwrites the stored currency of an existing bid unconditionally, and the ON CONFLICT branch writes `currency=excluded.currency`, so the unit of an already-stored amount is rewritten while the number is left alone. The legacy row this hits is the exact one the commit message exists because of: the old form offered KRW/USD/EUR/JPY and every tender created through the UI is KRW (web/src/pages/Objects.tsx:699 hardcodes it), so a bid stored as USD 50,000 against a KRW tender is the normal pre-change state. On the next save that row silently becomes KRW 50,000. Nothing warns the bidder or the buyer, there is no backfill, and the mismatch guard at sourcing.go:308 cannot catch it because the client now sends the tender's own code.

web/src/pages/Portal.tsx:779 `const currency = item.currency || "KRW"` takes the tender's code and ignores `response.currency`, so for that same legacy bid the form renders `총 견적금액 (KRW)` (Portal.tsx:820) directly above `defaultValue={response?.totalAmount}` = 50000, a number that was dollars. Before this change the box showed the bid's own currency (`defaultValue={response?.currency || "KRW"}`). This is a new, user-visible mislabeling of an existing amount, and it is what feeds the silent rewrite above.

internal/httpapi/currency_integration_test.go:23 the new integration test only covers a tender in USD with no prior bid; it never seeds a response whose currency differs from the tender's, which is the only case where the overwrite at sourcing.go:311 does anything. The behaviour that regressed is not exercised by any test in this branch.

web/src/pages/Approvals.tsx:150 and :202 still call `money(item.amount)` with no code, and internal/httpapi/workflows.go:261 does not select `o.currency`, so the approval inbox — the screen where someone authorizes the spend — still renders a USD purchase order as ₩. The commit message promises to "say which one every amount is in"; 11 of the 18 `money()` call sites were left unchanged, including this one and web/src/pages/Suppliers.tsx:1906. A Go-side sweep test was added for the write path but nothing holds the render path, which is where the ₩ mislabeling actually lives.
notes: Verified green on a throwaway Postgres 16: `go build ./...`, `go vet`, full `go test ./...` with VENDRA_TEST_DSN (internal/httpapi 22.5s ok), `npx tsc --noEmit`, and full `npx vitest run` (17 files, 72 tests). Both new integration tests pass and both genuinely fail on the pre-change code (validCurrencyFields does not exist on main; the portal test asserts `readonly` and the absence of the combobox). The new unit tests are real assertions, not no-ops.
No schema migration and no external state change — a revert is clean. Rows written under the newly-blessed codes would remain, which is harmless.

internal/httpapi/rows.go:637-646 argues that mixing currencies in one column produces "a total that is not a total", but analytics.go:655 still recomputes `annual_spend` as `SUM(amount)` across every currency and Suppliers.tsx:241/296/902/1178, SupplierNetwork.tsx:213, Dashboard.tsx:246 and Objects.tsx:1216/1307/1334/1382 all render those sums as ₩. The PR's own reasoning applies to code it does not touch.

objects.go:410 newly permits changing a tender's currency with no check for existing submitted bids, so a buyer can reinterpret every stored bid amount on that object after the fact. Related: approval routing matches `minAmount` (objects.go:509) against the raw amount with no currency, so an object corrected to USD routes on its bare number.

There is no UI to set or correct a business object's currency — Objects.tsx:699 and Portal.tsx:991 both hardcode `currency: "KRW"` — so the PATCH capability the commit message describes as the fix for "an order entered under the wrong currency" is reachable only through the API.
Scope is otherwise clean: every hunk is currency-related, no refactors, formatting churn or dependency bumps.
